turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come on in. What can I do for you?

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): It's the sneezing, doctor, and the itchy eyes and the runny nose. It comes every spring and I'm going through tissues like nobody's business, and the garden out the back is in full bloom which doesn't help one bit.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh it's been five years... no, six years, I was counting from the wrong summer. We moved in twenty nineteen and this is the sixth spring in the house, so six.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Only in the spring?

[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Only the spring, yes, from about March until June. The rest of the year I'm grand, not a sniffle, uh, which is why I left it so long, I kept thinking it would pass on its own.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Worse at any particular time?

[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): When I'm cutting the grass, or if I'm out in the garden in the evening, it goes mad altogether. Inside with the windows shut it's a small bit better, though the sneezing still comes in fits.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any wheeze?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No wheeze, no. I can walk the dog up the hill without getting tight, I was half afraid it was asthma but there's no whistle in the chest at all.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Cough?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough either. It's all in the nose and the eyes, um, the throat gets a bit scratchy from the dripping but I'm not coughing.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Both eyes?

[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Both eyes, they itch something fierce and they water, especially the left one in the mornings. I look like I've been crying at the school gate and it's mortifying, truly.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): On any treatment?

[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Ceterizine from the chemist, I take it sometimes, not every day. I thought the dose was twenty milligrams but no, it's ten milligrams, I was mixing it up with a painkiller I had years ago. When I do take it the sneezing eases a small bit but the eyes stay itchy.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anything else?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing else, I don't even take a vitamin. My sister is forever at me to take one but I don't, I forget them.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Drug allergies?

[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): None that I know of. My sister is allergic to dust though, she gets wheezy and her eyes swell, she's on a spray from her own GP, but I've never had a reaction to a medicine myself.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anyone else in the family?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No, just her. My parents are grand, no asthma, no hay fever, and my brother is the same, it's only herself with the dust.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. Blood pressure is one thirty-two over eighty-four... no, one twenty-eight over seventy-six. Pulse seventy-two. Oxygen ninety-eight percent.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Eyes are red, conjunctiva injected both sides. Nasal mucosa pale and boggy. Chest clear, no wheeze.

[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Is the redness bad? I've been rubbing them, I know I shouldn't, and I tried cold teabags last week which did nothing, and the chemist said not to use some old steroid drops I found in the press.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any stomach symptoms?

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No, stomach's perfect, I eat fine, no heartburn, no change in the bowel. I was going to mention the heartburn I had in pregnancy years ago but that's long gone, not relevant now I suppose.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): This is seasonal allergic rhinitis. Hay fever.

[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): I thought as much. My sister said the same at Easter, going on about dust mites and hoovering, err, but mine is only the spring so it has to be the pollen, the birch at the end of the road especially.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stop the cetirizine. Skin prick test with the nurse Thursday morning. No antihistamine from now until after that test.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Thursday morning, grand, I don't start until half ten so I'm free. Will I need to fast, or is it just the arm?
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): No fasting. Just the forearm. If the skin prick is borderline we'll do a specific IgE blood test.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): And if it's not borderline, do we still do the bloods or leave them?
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Leave them. After the test start loratadine ten milligrams once a day... no, fexofenadine, a hundred and eighty milligrams once a day.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Once a day, by mouth, even on days I feel grand? I was only taking the ceterizine sometimes so a daily tablet is a change for me.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Every day through the season. Olopatadine drops, one drop each eye twice a day, start those today.

[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Twice a day, both eyes, even the left that's worse? I'll keep them in the fridge if that's allowed, or does the chemist say room temperature, I always get mixed up with drops.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): Room temperature is fine. I'll see you in two weeks with the result.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): If it has not settled in six weeks, we'll arrange a sinus scan.

spec.situation: Sneezing, itchy eyes and runny nose every spring; takes cetirizine 'sometimes'; sister is allergic to dust; no wheeze; doctor changes antihistamine and adds eye drops.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.

bad.reason: Only drug/medicine allergies denied, not all allergies.
Heartburn omission is wrong; patient also says no current heartburn.
bad.text: gastrointestinal (status=negative, details=No current stomach symptoms, eating fine, no bowel change, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: Runny nose occurs only in spring from about March until June; rest of the year asymptomatic.
No chest tightness/exertional limitation: patient can walk the dog up the hill without getting tight.
Itchy eyes are severe ('itch something fierce').
Cetirizine provides only partial relief: sneezing eases a bit but the eyes remain itchy.
No other regular medicines or supplements ('nothing else, I don't even take a vitamin').
Drug allergies documented imprecisely: patient said 'None that I know of' and specifically no personal reaction to medicines, rather than no allergies of any kind.
Family history detail omitted: no asthma or hay fever in parents, brother unaffected; only sister has dust allergy.
Review of systems negative for heartburn as well as no current stomach symptoms/eating fine/no bowel change.
Diagnosis was stated definitively as 'seasonal allergic rhinitis. Hay fever,' not merely provisional.
